🚀 Quick Start - Developing a New Feature

1

Understand the Required Feature

Determine: Is it a Decorator? Handler? Provider? Tool?

Safe New Decorator | Careful New Endpoint

2

Feature Flag

Add flag in appsettings.json before any code

"FeatureFlags:EnableMyFeature": false
3

The Implementation

Create the required Class/Interface

If Decorator: Must implement ISmartQueryServiceV2

4

Registration

Register in Program.cs - place in correct stack position

5

Testing

Unit tests + Integration tests

Ensure Core is not affected (Backward compatibility)

6

Toggle On

Change flag to true in production

"FeatureFlags:EnableMyFeature": true

📁 Project Structure

WISC/ WISC.API/ Controllers/ UnifiedSmartQueryController.cs ← New Endpoints here AiChatController.cs Program.cs ← Register Decorators here WISC.AI.Mind/ Services/ PersonaEnhancedQueryService.cs ← Decorators here SecureSmartQueryService.cs SmartQueryServiceV2.cs ← FROZEN - DON'T TOUCH Handlers/ *IntentHandler.cs ← New Handlers here Providers/ *Provider.cs ← New Providers here WISC.Domain/ ← FROZEN - NEVER MODIFY

✅ Pre-Development Checklist

Before starting development

  • Determine feature type (Decorator/Handler/Provider/Tool)
  • Create Feature Flag in appsettings.json
  • Ensure Core won't be affected (SmartQueryServiceV2)
  • Plan Tests (Unit + Integration)
  • Ensure Backward Compatibility

📝 Practical Example: Batch Query Feature

Scenario

User wants to ask 3 questions at once instead of one by one

Step 1: Feature Flag

// appsettings.json { "FeatureFlags:EnableBatchQueries": false }

Step 2: New Decorator

// WISC.AI.Mind/Services/BatchQueryService.cs public class BatchQueryService : ISmartQueryServiceV2 { private readonly ISmartQueryServiceV2 _inner; private readonly IConfiguration _config; public async Task<SmartQueryResponseV2> ExecuteAsync(...) { // Check if batch mode if (!IsBatchRequest(request)) return await _inner.ExecuteAsync(request, ct); // NEW BEHAVIOR: Parallel execution var queries = ExtractQueries(request); var tasks = queries.Select(q => ExecuteSingleAsync(q)); var results = await Task.WhenAll(tasks); return MergeResults(results); } }

Step 3: New Endpoint

// UnifiedSmartQueryController.cs [HttpPost("batch")] [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BatchQueryResponse))] public async Task<ActionResult> BatchQueryAsync( [FromBody] BatchQueryRequest request) { // Validate batch size limit // Execute through service stack // Return aggregated results }

Step 4: Registration

// Program.cs - Add to decorator stack builder.Services.AddScoped<ISmartQueryServiceV2>(sp => { var innerService = sp.GetRequiredService<SmartQueryServiceV2>(); var securityWrapped = new SecureSmartQueryService(innerService, ...); var personaWrapped = new PersonaEnhancedQueryService(securityWrapped, ...); // NEW: Add Batch decorator (outermost) return new BatchQueryService(personaWrapped, config); });

Step 5: Test

[Fact] public async Task BatchQuery_ExecutesMultipleQueries() { // Arrange var request = new BatchQueryRequest { Queries = new[] { "Show Ahmed's balance", "Get today's transactions" } }; // Act var result = await _controller.BatchQueryAsync(request); // Assert Assert.Equal(2, result.Results.Count); }

⚠️ Do's and Don'ts

✅ DO's

  • ✅ Use Feature Flags for every new feature
  • ✅ Create Decorators instead of modifying Core
  • ✅ Write Tests before Implementation (TDD)
  • ✅ Maintain Backward Compatibility
  • ✅ Register Decorators in correct order
  • ✅ Document the Feature in WISC_DOCS

❌ DON'Ts

  • ❌ Touch SmartQueryServiceV2.ExecuteAsync
  • ❌ Modify Domain Entities
  • ❌ Add Cloud APIs (Offline policy)
  • ❌ Forget the Feature Flag
  • ❌ Create Breaking Changes
  • ❌ Add Decorators without registration

� Feature Flags Configuration

Feature Flags provide granular control over system behavior. All flags are defined in appsettings.json and checked at runtime by the respective services.

⚙️

appsettings.json Location

WISC/WISC.API/appsettings.json

Current Feature Flags

{ "FeatureFlags": { // === AI & LLM Features === "EnableOllamaLocal": true, // Use local Ollama (strict offline mode) "EnableVoiceProcessing": false, // Speech-to-text for Egyptian Arabic "EnableSmartTagPromptInjection": true, // Inject smart tags into LLM prompts "EnableSmartTagValidation": true, // Validate SQL against smart tags "EnableSmartTagTelemetry": true, // Log smart tag usage metrics "SmartTagTokenBudget": 300, // Max tokens for smart tag context // === Persona & UX Features === "Features:PersonaResponses": true, // Enable Arabic persona formatting "EnableThoughtStream": true, // SignalR real-time thought streaming // === Security Features === "EnableCrossTenantValidation": true, // Strict tenant isolation checks "EnableSqlInjectionGuards": true, // Block dangerous SQL keywords "EnableBusinessRuleValidation": true, // Validate against business rules // === Development & Debug === "DebugMode": false, // Enable verbose logging "EnableQueryPreview": true, // Show SQL before execution "EnableDetailedErrorMessages": false, // Include stack traces in errors (dev only) "EnableMockLlmResponses": false // Use mock LLM for testing (no Ollama needed) } }

Usage in Code

// Check feature flag in service public class PersonaEnhancedQueryService : ISmartQueryServiceV2 { private readonly IConfiguration _config; public async Task<SmartQueryResponseV2> ExecuteAsync(...) { // Check if feature is enabled var enablePersona = _config.GetValue<bool>("Features:PersonaResponses"); if (!enablePersona) { // Skip persona formatting, return raw response return await _inner.ExecuteAsync(request, ct); } // Apply persona enhancement var result = await _inner.ExecuteAsync(request, ct); result.Message = FormatInPersona(result.Message); return result; } }

🎯 Best Practices

  • Always set new flags to false by default
  • Use feature flags for any new functionality
  • Test with flag off before enabling in production
  • Document flag purpose in code comments
  • Remove obsolete flags after feature is stable
